rationale: Hapax in this corpus. Position in the body-inventory (stones / bones / X / of-the-body) requires a hard structural body-element parallel to bones. Etymology unclear; possibly related to a fragment/piece root (ⲗⲁϫ in Crum) or a Greek-derived term. Tentative.
Lycopolitan stative form, possibly from ϩⲱⲡ 'hide/be placed' or a related dwelling-verb. Subject is plural (the things hidden inside are envy and bodily disturbance). Confidence low.
Lycopolitan reflex of ϭⲟⲗ 'lie, deceit' — paralleling ⲛⲟⲩⲭ 'falsehood' (line 4) and ⲡⲁⲟⲉ (line 7). Common Coptic lexeme.
Standard Coptic ⲱⲧⲧ̄ 'doubt' (Crum). Lycopolitan with prosthetic ⲟ-vowel. The negated conjunctive ⲛⲩ̄ⲧⲙ̄ⲟⲱⲧⲧ describes the steadfastness of the wise man.
Lycopolitan verbal form of unidentified root, paired with ⲱⲧⲧ̄ 'doubt' as negated conjunctives in moral exhortation. Possibly causative ⲁ-ⲧⲣⲉ- on a dispute-verb. Confidence low.

proposed_english: he who shall come forth / depart
rationale: Future relative substantive on uncommon verb ⲟⲁⲗⲧ. Closing line of kephalaion suggests a sapiential statement about the faithful coming before the Lord. The verb may be Lyc. for ⲱⲗⲧ̄ (depart) or a related motion-verb. Confidence low.
Lycopolitan with indef. article ⲟⲩ-, likely from ⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'anger, wrath.' Confirmed by collocation with active hostility against the teacher (ⲍⲓ ⲩⲛⲉⲩⲧ ⲛⲁⲍⲣⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'with wrath before men').

Already in accumulated vocabulary as 'his heart's desire' from the New Man passage; here applied to the inner working of envy/Matter rather than the indwelling Mind.

rationale: Lycopolitan ⲥⲙ̄ⲡⲱϣⲁ 'be worthy, be fitting.' Standard Coptic deontic construction introducing exhortation.
